newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed higher on Thursday after a hesitant start.
Dealers said volumes were reasonably thin, although they noted buying interest in the 2005-2010 area.
"There was a buyers strike at the open, but business was moderate later during the session," said one dealer.
"Bund futures were carrying the load," said another dealer, after the Bund future contracts showed another strong performance.
The December Bund future rose to 101.71 near the close, after opening at 101.40 and closing at 101.37 yesterday.
"The rising bund futures show that the undertone remains good," said the dealer.
Another dealer said he had some doubts about the direction. "The short end is out of favour," he said.
This morning's Dutch third quarter GDP figure rose an expected 3.0 percent year-on-year.
"This figure had no impact on the market," said one dealer, adding it was a higher figure than the expected GDP growth figure for Germany.
Last week a German institute said the German economy would expand 1.25 percent this year.
"The Dutch figure is pretty big," the dealer said, but he added that fear for inflation was not a real problem.
The 6.25 July 1998 bond rose 0.04 to 104.16/24, yielding 3.54 percent bid.
The January 2006 was trading at 102.16/24 at the close, with a bid yield of 5.68 percent, versus 101.91/99 on Wednesday.
The spread of the 10-year bond versus the April 2006 Bund was steady at minus 7 basis points.
